---
title: "Size and momentum"
jupyter: python3
---

A stock's past returns may help explain its future returns. But the apparent
momentum effect could differ with size. Here we compare two ways to sort on
both characteristics.

## Measure momentum

For a portfolio held in month $t$, we measure size at the end of month $t-1$
and compound returns from months $t-12$ through $t-2$ to measure momentum.
Skipping month $t-1$ separates the momentum signal from the most recent return.
The holding-period outcome is the return in month $t$.

{{< include _monthly-characteristics.qmd >}}

## Summarize the characteristics

We first restrict attention to observations for which both characteristics are
available. These descriptive calculations do not use the holding-month return.

```{python}
signals = (
    characteristics
    .filter(pl.col("size").is_finite() & pl.col("momentum").is_finite())
    .with_columns(log_size=pl.col("size").log())
)

monthly_summary = (
    signals
    .group_by("month")
    .agg(
        stocks=pl.len(),
        median_momentum=pl.col("momentum").median(),
        corr_size_momentum=pl.corr("log_size", "momentum"),
    )
)

monthly_summary.select(
    avg_stocks=pl.col("stocks").mean().round(0),
    avg_median_momentum_pct=(100 * pl.col("median_momentum").mean()).round(2),
    avg_corr=pl.col("corr_size_momentum").mean().round(3),
)
```

The correlation is cross-sectional in each month; we give each month equal
weight. Persistence asks a different question: how closely does a stock's
momentum today resemble its own momentum at an earlier date? Match the dates
rather than shifting by a number of rows, so a stock missing a month does not
silently appear to have been observed in it.

```{python}
def momentum_persistence(months):
    past = signals.select(
        "permno",
        pl.col("month").dt.offset_by(f"{months}mo"),
        pl.col("momentum").alias("momentum_past"),
    )

    return (
        signals
        .join(past, on=["permno", "month"], validate="1:1")
        .group_by("month")
        .agg(correlation=pl.corr("momentum", "momentum_past"))
        .select(lag_months=pl.lit(months),
                months=pl.col("correlation").is_finite().sum(),
                average_corr=pl.col("correlation").filter(
                    pl.col("correlation").is_finite()
                ).mean().round(3))
    )

pl.concat([momentum_persistence(h) for h in [1, 3, 12]])
```

The 1- and 3-month comparisons share many underlying returns by construction.
A high correlation at short lags need not mean the same stock stays a winner
for long.

## Sort the stocks into portfolios

An **independent sort** finds size and momentum breakpoints separately in each
month. A **dependent sort** finds momentum breakpoints *within* each size
group. The second approach ranks firms against other firms of similar size.

As in AnomalyLab's three-group implementation, we use 30th and 70th percentile
cutoffs, with observations exactly on a cutoff assigned to the lower group.
For this comparison we drop observations with missing holding-month returns
before forming groups, as AnomalyLab does. In an investable backtest, form the
groups before checking which returns are available, then handle missing
returns separately.

```{python}
def sort_into_three(data, characteristic, by, group):
    x = pl.col(characteristic)
    low = x.quantile(0.30, interpolation="linear").over(by)
    high = x.quantile(0.70, interpolation="linear").over(by)

    return data.with_columns(
        pl.when(x <= low).then(1).when(x <= high).then(2).otherwise(3)
        .alias(group)
    )

sort_sample = signals.filter(pl.col("ret").is_finite())
size_groups = sort_into_three(sort_sample, "size", "month", "size_group")

independent = sort_into_three(size_groups, "momentum", "month", "momentum_group")
dependent = sort_into_three(
    size_groups, "momentum", ["month", "size_group"], "momentum_group"
)
```

## Compare the portfolio returns

For each sort, first compute the nine monthly returns. Then subtract the
low-momentum return from the high-momentum return within each size group.
The table averages those monthly spreads and reports percentage points per
month. Value weights are the market capitalizations used at formation.

```{python}
def portfolio_returns(groups):
    return (
        groups
        .group_by("month", "size_group", "momentum_group")
        .agg(
            equal_weighted=pl.col("ret").mean(),
            value_weighted=(pl.col("ret") * pl.col("size")).sum() / pl.col("size").sum(),
        )
    )

def momentum_spread(returns, design):
    keys = ["month", "size_group"]
    low = returns.filter(pl.col("momentum_group") == 1)
    high = returns.filter(pl.col("momentum_group") == 3)

    return (
        high
        .join(low, on=keys, suffix="_low", validate="1:1")
        .group_by("size_group")
        .agg(
            months=pl.len(),
            equal_weighted_pct=(
                100 * (pl.col("equal_weighted") - pl.col("equal_weighted_low")).mean()
            ).round(3),
            value_weighted_pct=(
                100 * (pl.col("value_weighted") - pl.col("value_weighted_low")).mean()
            ).round(3),
        )
        .with_columns(sort=pl.lit(design))
    )

independent_returns = portfolio_returns(independent)
dependent_returns = portfolio_returns(dependent)

(
    pl.concat([momentum_spread(independent_returns, "Independent"),
               momentum_spread(dependent_returns, "Dependent")])
    .select("sort", "size_group", "months", "equal_weighted_pct", "value_weighted_pct")
    .sort("sort", "size_group")
)
```

The two designs need not produce the same portfolios or spreads. The
independent design holds the absolute momentum thresholds fixed across size
groups; the dependent design fills each size group with roughly the same
proportions of low-, medium-, and high-momentum stocks.

## Track changes in momentum groups

The persistence correlations summarize how closely the *levels* of momentum
move together. A transition matrix asks instead how often a stock remains
in the same *group*. Assign each stock to a momentum group every month
using the same 30th and 70th percentile cutoffs, without conditioning on
the holding-month return.

Match the same stock exactly 12 calendar months later. The percentages are
conditional on having a momentum group in both months. We pool stock-month
pairs before calculating each row's shares, rather than averaging monthly
shares. A month with more matched stocks therefore gets more weight.

```{python}
momentum_groups = (
    sort_into_three(signals, "momentum", "month", "momentum_group")
    .select("permno", "month", "momentum_group")
)
at_start = momentum_groups.select(
    "permno", "month", start_group="momentum_group"
)
one_year_later = momentum_groups.select(
    "permno",
    pl.col("month").dt.offset_by("-12mo"),
    end_group="momentum_group",
)
transition_pairs = at_start.join(
    one_year_later, on=["permno", "month"], validate="1:1"
)

transition_matrix = (
    transition_pairs
    .group_by("start_group")
    .agg(
        pairs=pl.len(),
        low_pct=100 * (pl.col("end_group") == 1).mean(),
        middle_pct=100 * (pl.col("end_group") == 2).mean(),
        high_pct=100 * (pl.col("end_group") == 3).mean(),
    )
    .sort("start_group")
)
transition_matrix.with_columns(pl.col("low_pct", "middle_pct", "high_pct").round(1))
```

Each row shows where stocks starting in that group end up after a year.
The diagonal gives the percentage that remains in the same group. This is
not a measure of how many stocks drop out of the sample.

AnomalyLab also pools counts before dividing by the row totals, but it pairs
dates by position in the sequence of distinct observed months. That agrees
with a 12-month calendar match here because the sequence has no missing
months. In a panel with a missing month across all stocks, the calendar
join still matches observations exactly one year apart.

```{python}
#| include: false

import os

if checkout := os.environ.get("ANOMALYLAB_CHECKOUT"):
    import sys
    from pathlib import Path

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(checkout).expanduser().resolve(strict=True)))
    from anomalylab import Panel

    reference = Panel(
        sort_sample.select("permno", "month", "ret", "size", "momentum")
        .sort("month", "permno").to_pandas(),
        id="permno", time="month", frequency="M", ret="ret",
    )
    keys = ["month", "permno", "size_group", "momentum_group"]
    size_and_mom = {"size_g3": "size_group", "momentum_g3": "momentum_group"}
    for design, groups, returns in [
        ("independent", independent, independent_returns),
        ("dependent", dependent, dependent_returns),
    ]:
        expected = (
            reference.group("ret", "size", ["size", "momentum"], [3, 3], sort_type=design)
            .rename(columns=size_and_mom)[keys]
            .sort_values(keys[:2]).reset_index(drop=True)
        )
        actual = groups.select(keys).sort(keys[:2]).to_pandas()
        actual["month"] = actual["month"].dt.to_period("M")
        pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(actual, expected, check_dtype=False)

        ew, vw = reference.bivariate_analysis(
            endog="ret", weight="size", sort_var="size", core_var="momentum",
            sort_g=3, core_g=3, sort_type=design, factor_return=True,
        )
        actual = returns.to_pandas()
        actual["month"] = actual["month"].dt.to_period("M")

        for column, expected in [("equal_weighted", ew), ("value_weighted", vw)]:
            raw = expected.loc[expected.index.get_level_values("size").isin([1, 2, 3]),
                               [1, 2, 3]]
            result = actual.pivot(index=["month", "size_group"],
                                  columns="momentum_group", values=column)
            expected_index = raw.index.set_names(["month", "size_group"])
            assert set(result.index) == set(expected_index)
            matches = result.reindex(index=expected_index, columns=[1, 2, 3])
            np.testing.assert_allclose(matches.to_numpy(), raw.to_numpy(),
                                       rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
            ref_spread = expected.loc[
                expected.index.get_level_values("size").isin([1, 2, 3]), "H-L"
            ]
            np.testing.assert_allclose((matches[3] - matches[1]).to_numpy(),
                                       ref_spread.to_numpy(), rtol=0, atol=1e-12)

        print(f"{design}: matched {groups.height:,} assignments and "
              f"{returns.height} portfolio-months per weighting method.", file=sys.stderr)

    dates = signals["month"].unique().sort()
    month_numbers = dates.dt.year() * 12 + dates.dt.month()
    assert month_numbers.diff().drop_nulls().eq(1).all()
    persistence_reference = Panel(
        signals.select("permno", "month", "momentum").to_pandas(),
        id="permno", time="month", frequency="M",
    )
    expected = persistence_reference.transition_matrix(
        "momentum", group=3, lag=12, decimal=12
    ).astype(float)
    assert transition_matrix["start_group"].to_list() == [1, 2, 3]
    actual = transition_matrix.select("low_pct", "middle_pct", "high_pct").to_numpy()
    np.testing.assert_allclose(actual.sum(axis=1), 100, rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(actual / 100, expected.to_numpy(), rtol=0, atol=1e-12)
    print(f"Momentum transitions: matched all nine shares across "
          f"{transition_pairs.height:,} stock-month pairs.", file=sys.stderr)
```
